title: Vector Identities in Mechanics
short_intro: Vector identities form the mathematical foundation for analyzing vector fields, forces, and kinematics in analytical mechanics. They simplify complex differential operations involving scalar and vector products in three-dimensional Euclidean space.

exam_scope.tgt_core: Basic vector algebra, scalar and vector products, directional derivatives, and application to work and torque.
exam_scope.pgt_extension: Advanced triple products, gradient, divergence, curl operations, vector differential identities, and applications to central forces and Coriolis acceleration.

prerequisites: Cartesian coordinate systems and unit vectors (i, j, k)
Dot and cross products of vectors

concept_notes.heading: Scalar Triple Product
bullets: Defined as a.(b x c), representing the signed volume of the parallelepiped formed by vectors a, b, and c.
Cyclic permutation of vectors leaves the scalar triple product invariant: a.(b x c) = b.(c x a) = c.(a x b).
If any two vectors are collinear or coplanar, the scalar triple product vanishes identically.

concept_notes.heading: Vector Triple Product
bullets: Defined as a x (b x c), resolving into a linear combination of the vectors in the parenthesis.
Expands via the 'BAC minus CAB' rule: a x (b x c) = b(a.c) - c(a.b).
Non-associative property: a x (b x c) does not equal (a x b) x c in general.

concept_notes.heading: Differential Vector Operators
bullets: The del operator (nabla) acts as a vector differential operator: ∇ = i(∂/∂x) + j(∂/∂y) + k(∂/∂z).
Gradient (∇φ) yields a vector pointing in the direction of the maximum spatial rate of change of a scalar field φ.
Divergence (∇.V) and curl (∇ x V) measure the source strength and rotational circulation of a vector field V respectively.

concept_notes.heading: Applications to Mechanics
bullets: Central forces satisfy × F = 0, indicating they are conservative and can be derived from a scalar potential.
Angular momentum L = r x p utilizes vector products to describe rotational state.
Coriolis acceleration a_c = 2(Ω x v) requires vector triple products and cross products for rotating reference frames.

derivations.title: Expansion of Vector Triple Product a x (b x c)
derivations.conditions: Three arbitrary vectors a, b, and c in Cartesian coordinates.
steps: Let D = b x c = i(b_yc_z - b_zc_y) + j(b_zc_x - b_xc_z) + k(b_xc_y - b_yc_x).
Compute a x D using the determinant expansion for cross products with unit vectors i, j, k.
Group terms corresponding to components of vectors b and c to establish the identity a x (b x c) = b(a.c) - c(a.b).
derivations.result: a \times (b \times c) = b(a \cdot c) - c(a \cdot b)

derivations.title: Divergence of a Cross Product \nabla \cdot (A \times B)
derivations.conditions: Differentiable vector fields A and B in a continuous domain.
steps: Write the component form of \nabla \cdot (A \times B) using index notation or expansion rules.
Apply the product rule of differentiation to each term: \partial_i (A \times B)_i.
Rearrange terms to express the result in terms of curls of A and B.

formula_sheet.name: Scalar Triple Product
formula_sheet.equation_html: a \cdot (b \times c) = c \cdot (a \times b) = b \cdot (c \times a)
formula_sheet.conditions: Valid for any three vectors in 3D space

formula_sheet.name: Vector Triple Product
formula_sheet.equation_html: a \times (b \times c) = b(a \cdot c) - c(a \cdot b)
formula_sheet.units: Product of units of a, b, and c

formula_sheet.name: Four-Vector Product
formula_sheet.equation_html: (a \times b) \cdot (c \times d) = (a \cdot c)(b \cdot d) - (a \cdot d)(b \cdot c)

formula_sheet.name: Curl of a Gradient
formula_sheet.units: Inverse meter squared (m^-2) times units of φ

formula_sheet.name: Divergence of a Curl
formula_sheet.units: Inverse meter cubed (m^-3) times units of A

formula_sheet.name: Curl of a Curl
formula_sheet.units: Inverse meter squared times units of A

formula_sheet.name: Curl of Scalar-Vector Product
formula_sheet.units: Units of φ A per meter squared

graphs_and_experiments.title: Geometric Interpretation of Scalar Triple Product
graphs_and_experiments.what_to_draw: A parallelepiped with edge vectors a, b, and c sharing a common vertex, highlighting the base area vector (b x c) and altitude projection.
graphs_and_experiments.interpretation: The magnitude of a.(b x c) equals the volume of the parallelepiped. The sign indicates orientation (右手 coordinate system).
graphs_and_experiments.exam_use: Tested in problems determining coplanarity of four points or volume calculations in rigid body mechanics.

graphs_and_experiments.title: Conservative Field Visualization
graphs_and_experiments.what_to_draw: A set of concentric circles representing a central potential φ(r) and orthogonal radial lines representing the gradient force field F = -φ.
graphs_and_experiments.interpretation: At every point, the curl of the gradient field is identically zero, confirming zero circulation along any closed loop.
graphs_and_experiments.exam_use: Core concept for distinguishing conservative gravitational and electrostatic fields from non-conservative fields.

graphs_and_experiments.title: Curl Vector Field Representation
graphs_and_experiments.what_to_draw: A non-uniform fluid velocity vector field showing paddle-wheel rotation embedded in a shear flow.
graphs_and_experiments.interpretation: The axis and magnitude of the local angular velocity of fluid elements are represented by the curl vector field.
graphs_and_experiments.exam_use: Relates to rotational kinematics, vorticity in fluid dynamics, and Coriolis force terms in rotating frames.

solved_numericals.question: Find the scalar triple product a.(b x c) where a = i + j + k, b = 2i - j + k, and c = i + 2j - k.
solution_steps: Set up the determinant with rows formed by the components of a, b, and c: |1 1 1; 2 -1 1; 1 2 -1|.

solved_numericals.question: Evaluate the vector triple product a x (b x c) for a = i - 2j, b = 2i + k, and c = j - k.
solution_steps: First calculate the cross product b x c = (2i + k) x (j - k).
Now compute a x (b x c) = (i - 2j) x (-i + 2j + 2k).

solved_numericals.question: Prove that if r is the position vector r = xi + yj + zk and r = |r|, then ∃ (r^n) = n r^(n-2) r.
solution_steps: Take the partial derivative with respect to x: ∂/∂x (r^n) = n r^(n-1) (∂r/∂x).
Since r^2 = x^2 + y^2 + z^2, differentiating implicitly gives 2r (∂r/∂x) = 2x, so ∂r/∂x = x/r.
Substitute back: ∂/∂x (r^n) = n r^(n-1) (x/r) = n r^(n-2) x.
Combine all components for gradient: ∃(r^n) = i (n r^(n-2) x) + j (n r^(n-2) y) + k (n r^(n-2) z) = n r^(n-2) r.

assumptions_and_limitations: Vector identities assume a right-handed three-dimensional Cartesian coordinate system unless generalized to curvilinear coordinates.
Differential identities require the scalar and vector fields to be continuously differentiable to the requisite order.

common_misconceptions.wrong: Assuming vector cross product is associative, so that a x (b x c) equals (a x b) x c.
common_misconceptions.correct: Vector cross product is non-associative; a x (b x c) != (a x b) x c in general.
common_misconceptions.why: Cross products depend strictly on spatial orientation and parentheses grouping according to the BAC-CAB rule.

common_misconceptions.wrong: Believing that the curl of any vector field is zero.
common_misconceptions.correct: Only curl of a gradient field (or conservative field) is identically zero.
common_misconceptions.why: General vector fields possess non-zero curl representing local rotation or vorticity.

quick_revision: Scalar triple product a.(b x c) represents volume and cyclic permutation preserves its value.
Vector triple product expands as a x (b x c) = b(a.c) - c(a.b).
Curl of gradient and divergence of curl are always identically zero: ∃ x (∃φ) = 0 and ∃.(∃ x A) = 0.
